sentences.text:
This judgment is emerged consequent upon the petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of M.V. Act,
claiming compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/- on account of the death of Mohana H., in the road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioners, in brief, is as follows:
On 14-06-2023 at about 2.15 a.m. early morning, the deceased was traveling in a Ertiga Car bearing No.KA-05-MR-4170 on Tumkuru-Madugiri SH33 road, near Jatti Agrahara village C.N. Durga Hobli, Kortagere Taluk, Tumkuru slowly and cautiously on extreme left side of the said road, near Jatti Agrahara village, C.N. Durga Hobli,
Kortagere Taluk, Tumkuru, at that time all of a sudden the Ashok Leyland Goods Carrier bearing Reg. No.KA-09-AA-3919 drove by its driver at high speed rash and negligent manner without observing norms from opposite direction of the deceased vehicle dashed against the Car of the deceased and caused the accident.
Due to the impact, deceased sustained grievous injuries to his head.

Immediately the injured was shifted to Victoria hospital, wherein first aid treatment was given and the doctor after examination declared that the injured was already dead due to the accidental injuries.
Thereafter postmortem was conducted and handed over the body to the petitioners and they have performed funeral and obsequies ceremonies by spending Rs.3,00,000/-.

Prior to the accident, deceased was hale and healthy, aged about 34 years and working as Field Officer at Arthika Saksharatha Kendra Center for Financial Literacy,
Kortagere and earning Rs.20,000/ per month and contributing his entire income for the maintenance of his family.

sentences.text: Due to the untimely death of deceased the petitioners have suffered mentally and financially.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are the owner and insurer of the offending Lorry are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Accordingly, prays to award compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/- with interest to the petitioners.

sentences.text: In spite of service of summons, the respondent No.1-owner has remained absent, hence placed exparte.
After service of summons, the respondent No.2- insurer has appeared before the tribunal through its counsel and filed written statement.

Respondent No.2 - insurance company appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by admitting the issuance of policy in respect of Lorry bearing No.KA-09-AA-3919 and the liability if any is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
It is contended that the non-compliance of Sec.158(6) of the MV Act.
Further contended that, the offending lorry driver was not having valid and effective DL at the time of accident and the offending vehicle was also not having FC and permit at the time of accident.
Further it is contended that the accident occurred on account of use of two vehicles, as such held guilty of composite negligence.
Further it is submitted that the owner and insurer of the Ertiga Car bearing No.KA-05-MR-4170 were not made as parties, as such prays to dismiss the petitioner for non-joinder of necessary parties.
It has denied the age, occupation and income of the deceased.
Further it has denied the cause and manner of accident and the involvement of the offending lorry in the said accident.
Hence the respondent No.2 - insurance company prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contentions, the following issues were framed by this court:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioners prove that deceased Mohana H. S/o Hanumanthappa B.P.
sustained injuries due to rash and negligent act of driving of Ashoka Leyland Lorry bearing No.KA-09-AA-3919 dated 14.06.2023 at about 2.15 a.m. and succumbed to the injuries ?
2. Whether the petitioners prove the age and earnings of the deceased as stated in the claim petition?
3. Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Mohana H.
S/o Hanumanthappa B.P.?
4. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from whom?
5. What order or award?
5. In order to prove the claim petition, the 1st petitioner is examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.14.
On the other hand 2nd respondent has examined Head Constable at Sira Town station as RW.1.

7. My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1 : In the affirmative,
 Issue No.2 : In the affirmative,
 Issue No.3 : In the affirmative,

In the affirmative  Issue No.5 : As per final orders  for the following.-

REASONS ISSUE NO.1:
8.

The petitioners to prove their claim have produced true copies of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar,
spot sketch, IMV report, inquest report, PM report and charge sheet, which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 8.
9.
As per the documents, Ex.P1 FIR is came to be registered on the basis of the complaint given by one Shashidhar who is eyewitness of the accident as per Ex.P2.
In the Ex.P2, he has alleged the rash and negligent driving by the driver of Lorry bearing No.KA-09-AA-3919.
After the registration of FIR the IO conducted the spot mahazar and spot sketch as per Ex.P3 and P.4.
As per the spot mahazar and sketch marked at Ex.P3 & P.4 the accident spot is in the left side portion of the road in which the car bearing No.KA-05-MR-4170 was proceeding.

10. The Ex.P.5 IMV report shows that the Car of the deceased has got damages in its front shape totally damaged, front wind screen glass, front engine bonnet, cooling system, steering system,
electrical wiring system, front dash board, front both side wheels, front chassis, front motor vehicle top hood and all seats are damaged.
On the other hand, the offending lorry bearing No.KA-09- AA-3919 has got damages in its front right side bumper, front right side head light assembly, front right side wheel fender.
Thus, it is found that as per Ex.P3 mahazar P.4 sketch and Ex.P.5, the offending lorry has came to the right side portion of the road and caused the accident.
The driver of the offending lorry came to the wrong side of the road and thereby caused the accident.

The Ex.P.3 to 5 evidentiates that the driver of the the lorry bearing No.KA-09-AA-3919 came to his wrong side I..e, right side portion of the road without observing the vehicles coming from the opposite side and caused the accident.
If, the driver of the lorry bearing No.KA-09-AA-3919 not came to the wrong side of the road, the alleged accident was not going to be caused.

Thereby the Ex.P3 to 5 mahazar,
sketch and IMV report helped the petitioners to prove the alleged negligence of the driver of the lorry bearing No.KA-09-AA-3919.
11.
The respondent No.1 owner of the lorry bearing No.KA-09-AA-3919 neither appeared before the tribunal nor produced any evidence or documents in support of his case.

The respondent No.2 filed written by denying the negligence on the part of the offending lorry and also examined Head Constable of Sira Town Station as RW1 who deposed that he has received the complaint from one Shashidara S/o Srinivasaiah and registered FIR in Crime No.153/2023 of Kortagere Police station and after registering the FIR the file was handed over to their inspector Sri Suresh.

sentences.text: 12. Ex.P6 is the inquest and Ex.P7 is the postmortem report where both these documents discloses that the deceased succumbed due to head injury sustained in the said accident.

13. It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

entities.text: Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105,
where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the rider of the offending van.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105

sentences.text: 14. In view of the ratio laid down in the authorities referred to above and applying the settled principle of law to the case at hand, which is further supported by the oral and documentary evidence adduced by PW-1, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident leading to this case indeed occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of offending Lorry bearing No.KA-09-AA-3919 resulting in deceased sustaining injuries.
15. Ex.P8 is the charge sheet filed against the driver of the offending Lorry bearing No.KA-09-AA-3919 for the offence punishable under Sec. 279, 337, 338 & 304 (A) of IPC.
The investigating officer as per Ex.P8 charge sheet opined that the driver of offending Lorry bearing No.KA- 09-AA-3919 driven the said vehicle in a rash and negligent manner.
No other evidence is placed by the respondents to show the contributory negligence by the deceased.
During the course of cross-examination of PW.1, nothing has been elicited so as to disprove the case of the petitioners.
16. As per well settled position of law the standard of proof in claim petition like present one, is only preponderance of probabilities.

Looking to the oral as well as documentary evidence of the petitioners there are sufficient materials to show that Mohana H. died in the accident dated 14-06-2023 which is caused by the driver of the Lorry bearing No.KA-09-AA-3919.
Accordingly issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.
ISSUE NO.3 17.
As held herein above, the petitioners have proved that Mohana H. died on 14-06-2023 due to the injuries sustained in RTA, which is caused by the driver of the respondent No.1.

sentences.text: As contended in the petition the petitioners are the parents and unmarried sister of the deceased Mohana H..
The respondents do not specifically deny the relationship of petitioners with deceased.
The petitioners to prove their relationship with the deceased, have produced the notarized copies of Aadhar cards of petitioners which are marked under Ex.P9 to P.12.
During the course of recording the evidence the notarized copies of Aadhar cards are compared with the original documents and found correct.
The respondents do not dispute the Aadhar cards produced by the petitioners.
The respondent No.2 has not adduced any evidence to disprove the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.
The petitioner No.3 being the blind and visually impaired certainly depend on her brother.

19. In the absence of contradictory evidence the evidence of the petitioner is to be accepted and it is considered that, petitioners are the parents and sister of deceased being the dependents are entitled for compensation.
Accordingly Issue No.3 is answered in the Affirmative.

Issue No.2 & 4 :
20.

The issued No.1 & 2 are answered in the affirmative by holding that the deceased Mohana H.
died in the RTA dated 14-06-2023 caused by the negligence driving by the driver of Lorry bearing No.KA-09-AA-3919 and the petitioners are entitled for the compensation.
21. Now the quantum of compensation is to be decided.
In the Aadhar card of the deceased Mohana H. produced at Ex.P9, the date of birth of the deceased is shown as 04-07-1989 and the accident was occurred on 14-06-2023.
If it is considered, as on the date of the accident the age of the deceased was 34 years.
22. As stated in the petition deceased was working as a Field Officer at Arthika Saksharatha Kendra Center for Financial Literacy Kortagere and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.

sentences.text: To know the exact income of the deceased except said account statement no other documents are produced by the petitioners.

As per the table quoted above the deceased got Rs.42,840/- in the month of January-2023, in the month of February 2023 Rs.13,500/-, in the month of March-2023 Rs.43,670/-, in the month of April- 2023 Rs.21,840/-, in the month of May-2023 Rs.23,740/-, in the month of June-2023 Rs.8,000/- from DHAN Foundation.
The deceased met with an accident on 14.06.2023 and died on the same day.
By relying on the above quoted table the petitioner use to get Rs.21,840/- to Rs.43,670/- from DHAN Foundation from January 2023 to May-2023.

Hence, the same is considered the income of the deceased and average income of the deceased is taken as Rs.22,000/-
23.
As per Sarala varma's case the proper multiplier applicable to the age of deceased is 16.

Since the deceased was a bachelor 50% of the income is to be deducted towards his personal expenses, then the total loss of dependency would be Rs.21,12,000/- (Rs.22,000/- X 12 x 16 = Rs.42,24,000/-
minus half of the income i.e., 21,12,000/-) = Rs.21,12,000/-).

24. In Civil Special leave petition (Civil No.25590/2014 dated 31.10.2016 (National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi & others), the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that "While determining the income, in case the deceased was self- employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi & others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."
26. As per the above decisions 40% out of loss of dependency has to be granted towards future prospects which would Rs.8,44,800/-.
LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:
27. The Petitioners are the Parents and unmarried sister of the deceased and they have lost their loving daughter.
Therefore they are entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/- (Rs.40,000/- x 10% hike every three years from 2017 as per Pranay Sethi Case) under the head of loss of consortium.

28. Further I inclined to award Rs.16,500/- towards loss of estate and Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses (this amount is calculated as per Pranaya Sethi case with enhanced rate at 10% after three years).

The petitioners are entitled for compensation under the following heads:
1. Loss of dependency Rs. 21,12,000/-
2. Loss of future prospects Rs. 8,44,800/-
3. Loss of consortium Rs. 1,32,000/-
4. Funeral expenses Rs. 16,500/-
5. Transport of dead body Rs. 16,500/-
Total Rs
29. Liability:-
In the petition it is alleged that the respondent No.1& 2 are the owner and insurer of the Lorry bearing No.KA-09-AA-3919.
The respondent No.2 in its written statement has admitted the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle.
No other grounds are made out to show the violation of policy conditions by respondent No.1 owner.
As discussed above, the petitioners successfully proved the negligence on the part of the driver of Lorry bearing No.KA-09-AA-3919.
The respondent No.2 failed to show that the contributory negligence by the deceased.
Thereby, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer are liable to pay the compensation along with the interest.

Hence, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and the respondent No.2 insurance company shall indemnify the compensation on behalf of the respondent No.1.
The petitioners are entitled for the interest at 6% per annum.
Accordingly, this Issue No.2 and 4 answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.4:-
30.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.31,21,800/- (Rupees Thirty one lakhs twenty one thousand eight hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,. from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.2 - insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
The petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for the compensation at the ratio of 20:40:40.
